Account Factory provisions and enrolls accounts into a governed landing zone using standardized account settings.
Execute the established provisioning workflow with the approved account inputs and inspect the account’s enrollment and organizational-unit placement.
Verify the supplied baseline checkpoints against the account’s applied controls; creating an account alone does not demonstrate governance completion.
A virtual environment isolates the Python interpreter context and installed packages used by an application.
Create one with python -m venv ENV_DIR and activate it using the platform’s activation command, such as source ENV_DIR/bin/activate on Unix.
Install supplied dependencies with python -m pip install -r requirements.txt inside the environment, inspect them with python -m pip list, and run the supplied script with that interpreter.
Confirm the approved AWS profile and Region through the supplied credential configuration before running AWS automation.
The AWS CLI automatically follows service-side pagination for supported commands unless automatic pagination is disabled.
Use an explicit --profile and --region with --output json for structured inventory and avoid --no-paginate when the full listing is required.

--page-size changes service-call page size rather than the total output count; --max-items limits output and a returned NextToken must be resumed with --starting-token when manually collecting the remainder.
A runbook documents procedures for a known operational outcome and should be usable by the operator performing the task.
Write the task’s preconditions, ordered actions and expected results so execution can be checked rather than inferred.
Include failure-handling and escalation instructions identifying when routine execution must stop and who takes over.
A Pod groups containers with shared networking and storage and has a lifecycle distinct from the controller that may replace it.
Pod phases include Pending, Running, Succeeded, Failed and Unknown; phase alone is not a complete diagnosis of container health.
Use kubectl get pod NAME, kubectl describe pod NAME and kubectl logs NAME -c CONTAINER to inspect status, scheduling or runtime events and container output.
An RDS DB instance has an identifier, engine, endpoint and operational status that can be inspected in the console or through describe-db-instances.
Inspect the intended DB instance and verify its engine and status before attempting the supplied database connection.
Connect using the supplied endpoint, database client and approved credentials, then run the supplied query to check the data marker; instance status alone does not verify application data.
S3 versioning retains multiple versions of an object, including versions displaced by overwrites.
In a versioning-enabled bucket, a simple delete ordinarily creates a delete marker rather than removing prior versions; deleting a specified version permanently removes it.
To restore an overwritten object, copy the selected prior version to the same key to create a new current version; to undo a simple deletion, remove its delete marker to expose the preceding version.
Inspect noncurrent-version expiration and other lifecycle rules so required recoverable versions remain for the required window.

Enable versioning in the S3 console under the bucket’s Properties > Bucket Versioning > Edit > Enable > Save changes, and check its Bucket Versioning setting; apply the supplied lifecycle JSON with aws s3api put-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket <bucket> --lifecycle-configuration file://<policy.json>, then retrieve it with aws s3api get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket <bucket> to verify the configured rules.
ECR stores container images in repositories and assigns image digests that identify image content.
Authenticate Docker with aws ecr get-login-password --region REGION piped to docker login --username AWS --password-stdin REGISTRY.
Tag the already-built image with REGISTRY/REPOSITORY:TAG and run docker push with that reference.
Use docker pull REGISTRY/REPOSITORY@sha256:DIGEST to retrieve the exact image and verify publisher and consumer access with their approved identities.
An artifact attestation binds provenance such as source repository, revision and build workflow to an artifact digest.

For a supplied output file, set workflow permissions id-token: write, contents: read and attestations: write, generate provenance with actions/attest@v4 and subject-path set to the file, then publish it with actions/upload-artifact@v4 using path set to that file and name set to the supplied revision-based version; retain the workflow run, artifact name and upload’s SHA256 digest as the immutable content reference, since v4 artifacts are immutable.

Download the published artifact with actions/download-artifact, which checks the upload’s SHA256 digest and warns on mismatch, then verify the extracted output file’s provenance with gh attestation verify PATH/TO/YOUR/BUILD/ARTIFACT-BINARY -R ORGANIZATION_NAME/REPOSITORY_NAME --format json and inspect the verified attestation for the source revision and build workflow/run before deployment.
A CloudFormation template’s Resources section declares resources by logical ID, Type and Properties.
An S3 bucket declaration uses Type: AWS::S3::Bucket; Ref on its logical ID returns its bucket name.
Modify the supplied declared property and references, validate with aws cloudformation validate-template --template-body file://TEMPLATE, and create the sandbox stack from the approved template.
Inspect stack events and outputs and the bucket’s live property to confirm the declaration was deployed.
Secrets Manager stores protected secret values and returns them to authorized consumers at runtime.
Retrieve a secret through GetSecretValue using the supplied secret identifier and approved runtime identity, with secretsmanager:GetSecretValue permission.
Use the retrieved value in the runtime consumer without writing it into source code or logs; verify success through the consumer’s safe result rather than displaying the value.
Continuous improvement uses feedback and measured outcomes to identify and address delivery friction.
Identify a bottleneck supported by the supplied delivery evidence and propose one bounded change with a measurable expected outcome.
Compare the success signal before and after the change to determine whether the intervention improved the intended outcome.
AWS Config rules evaluate recorded resource configuration against desired conditions and report compliance results.
Open the rule’s noncompliant resources and inspect the affected resource, evaluation result and rule parameters to identify the configuration mismatch.
Choose the established remediation or escalation path from the governing policy rather than treating a compliance result as proof of an attack.
CloudFormation drift detection compares supported explicitly declared resource properties with their current values.
Run drift detection on the provisioned stack after the supplied out-of-band change, wait for completion and inspect the bucket’s expected and actual property values.
Drift detection reports differences without repairing them; unsupported or undeclared properties may not be checked.
CloudFormation stack events record resource operation status and failure reasons during an update.
After the supplied controlled update failure, inspect the first failing resource event and subsequent rollback events.
UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE indicates rollback to the previous working stack state; UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED requires resolving the rollback failure before continuing.
An instance profile contains one IAM role and provides a way to pass that role to EC2.
Attach or replace the approved instance profile on the EC2 instance using the instance’s IAM-role setting or associate-iam-instance-profile.
Use the instance’s role credential provider rather than embedded keys, inspect the caller identity and test one allowed and one denied operation under the assigned role’s permissions.
EKS Pod Identity associates a Kubernetes service account in a namespace and cluster with an IAM role for application AWS access.
Create an association for the supplied cluster, namespace, service account and approved role; run the workload with that serviceAccountName.

The Pod Identity agent and supported SDK credential chain supply temporary role credentials to associated Pods; verify allowed access from the intended workload and rejection from an unassociated workload.
GitHub Actions OIDC enables a workflow to obtain temporary AWS role credentials without storing AWS access keys.
Configure the GitHub token issuer as an IAM OIDC provider and constrain the role trust policy’s aud and sub claims to the approved audience and repository/branch or environment.
Give the workflow id-token: write permission and configure the AWS credential action to assume the approved role; test that an unapproved repository or branch cannot assume it.
Temporary AWS credentials consist of an access key ID, secret access key and session token and expire after their issued lifetime.
Call aws sts assume-role with --role-arn, --role-session-name and the approved --duration-seconds, then use all three returned credential fields and inspect Expiration.

Permissions granted through a role’s identity-based policies are intersected with any session policies; resource-based grants are evaluated separately, and grants directly to the session ARN are not limited by session policies; an explicit deny in any applicable policy overrides an allow.
EventBridge target execution authority is separate from the event pattern that selects events.
For targets requiring an execution role, grant events.amazonaws.com permission to assume the role and attach permissions scoped to the approved target operation and resource.
Targets such as SNS and Lambda use resource-based permissions for invocation; use the target’s required authorization model rather than assuming every target uses a role.
A Config managed rule evaluates supported resource configuration against the rule’s criteria and configured parameters.
Choose the supplied rule, resource scope and parameters, run or inspect its evaluation, and compare compliant and noncompliant sample resources.
Read each evaluation’s resource ID and compliance result rather than treating the presence of the rule as proof that all resources passed.
An AWS budget compares cost or usage with a configured budget amount over a selected period.
Create a cost budget with the approved scope, amount and period, then configure an actual or forecast threshold and approved notification recipient.
A notification alerts its recipients; stopping resources requires separately configured actions rather than the notification itself.
A buildspec is a YAML document describing build commands and artifacts; version: 0.2 supports commands in the same shell environment.
Place supplied commands under phases such as install, pre_build, build and post_build, using commands lists in the needed phases.
Set artifacts.files and, if needed, base-directory to match the generated output, then inspect the build’s phase logs and exported artifact.
For EC2 deployments, appspec.yml maps revision files to destinations and lists scripts for deployment lifecycle hooks.
Configure the supplied application and deployment group to identify the intended EC2 targets and revision, with the approved service role and installed agent.
Inspect the AppSpec files mapping and hooks, execute the supplied deployment action and verify hook results and application files on the target.
Target tracking adjusts Auto Scaling capacity to keep a chosen metric near its target value.
Select the approved metric and target value and configure instance warmup along with the group’s minimum, desired and maximum capacities.
Run the bounded load test and compare metric values and scaling activities with resulting capacity; capacity cannot exceed the group’s configured maximum.
An ECR repository policy grants specified principals repository operations such as pulling images or uploading image layers.
Scope the supplied policy’s principals and actions to approved publishers and consumers, then test push and pull and an unapproved principal.
ECR authentication also requires ecr:GetAuthorizationToken through an identity policy; repository permissions alone do not grant that action.
ECR lifecycle policies select images using criteria such as tag status and count or age and expire matching images.
Use rulePriority, selection and action fields to express the supplied retention policy and run a lifecycle preview before applying it.
Check previewed digests against deployed versions; exclude still-needed versions from eligible expiry rather than assuming deployment makes an image immune to lifecycle rules.
An Application Load Balancer listener evaluates routing rules and forwards matching requests to a target group.
Configure the supplied listener protocol and port, forwarding rule and registered target protocol/port, then test the endpoint.
Configure the health-check path, port and success codes to match the backend and inspect target health reasons when a request path fails.
An ALB normally routes to healthy registered targets, but when every registered target in a target group is unhealthy it fails open and routes to those unhealthy targets.
CloudWatch log-group retention controls how long events remain; by default logs are retained indefinitely.
Set the supplied retention interval with put-retention-policy and inspect the log group’s retentionInDays.
Expired events are marked for deletion; physical deletion typically takes up to 72 hours, so expiry is not necessarily immediate disappearance.
An RDS DB snapshot captures the database instance for later restoration.
Create a manual snapshot for the intended DB instance and wait until its snapshot status is available.
Restore the snapshot to a new DB instance identifier using the supplied network settings; restoration creates a separate instance rather than overwriting the source.
Wait for the restored instance to become available, connect to its endpoint and run the supplied query to verify the recovery marker.
CloudWatch Logs uses IAM policies to authorize log-group and log-stream operations.
Grant the approved reader the required read actions on the intended log-group resources and remove unnecessary broader grants; some operations require resource scope *.
Test the approved and unapproved principals against the intended read operations because collecting logs does not itself grant reader access.
An ECS task definition specifies the image and container runtime settings for tasks.
Set containerDefinitions entries with name, image, portMappings, cpu and memory settings appropriate to the supplied launch type, and register the task definition.
Run the registered task definition with the supplied cluster and network configuration, then inspect task status and container details to verify the image and runtime settings.
An access-denied diagnosis is specific to the requesting principal, operation, resource and request context.
Inspect the request and applicable policies for an explicit deny, missing allow or unsatisfied condition and use available denial context to localize the cause.
Resource policies, session policies, permissions boundaries and organization policies can constrain access beyond one identity policy; explicit deny takes precedence.
Make the smallest approved policy or request correction supported by the evidence and retest the denied operation.
terraform apply PLAN_FILE executes the changes recorded in a saved plan without generating a new plan or prompting for approval.
Use the supplied approved saved plan file rather than an unplanned apply, and retain the apply outcome as execution evidence.
Inspect terraform show PLAN_FILE and the resulting resource or outputs to check that the created EC2 instance matches the approved plan.
Run Command executes Systems Manager documents on managed nodes under authorized access.
Use send-command with the supplied document and explicit approved --instance-ids or tag-based --targets and document parameters.
Record the command ID and inspect each invocation’s status and output; the parent command status does not replace per-node result checks.
terraform validate checks configuration syntax and internal consistency without checking remote service state or provider API success.
Initialize needed providers and modules with terraform init -backend=false before static validation where backend access is not needed.
Run terraform validate as a blocking workflow step; stop on its nonzero exit result, correct the invalid declaration and rerun before the supplied approved apply step.

optional_enrichment.statement: As optional supporting practice, terraform fmt -check checks canonical formatting and can be used as an additional blocking configuration check.

required_facts.statement: AWS SDK retries cover selected transient or throttling errors rather than making every failed request safe to repeat.

Set botocore.config.Config(retries={"mode": "standard", "total_max_attempts": APPROVED_ATTEMPTS}) on the supplied Boto3 client to bound requests with the SDK’s backoff; do not wrap terminal errors in an unbounded retry loop.

Catch botocore.exceptions.ClientError around the supplied call, inspect its response["Error"]["Code"] and response["Error"]["Message"] and preserve response["ResponseMetadata"]["RequestId"] when present; report the terminal failure or exhausted retry outcome.
When configuring Boto3, total_max_attempts includes the initial request, whereas max_attempts in a Config object counts retries after the initial request.
Cost Explorer analyzes billed cost and usage for selected time intervals and grouping dimensions.
Filter the supplied period and account, group by service or usage type, and inspect the cost and usage values to identify the supported cost driver.
Use the billed usage evidence to justify the avoidable charge rather than equating the existence of a resource with a specific charge.
A Deployment manages ReplicaSets to reconcile the requested Pod replicas and Pod template.
Apply the supplied Deployment with kubectl apply -f FILE and inspect kubectl get deployment NAME and the associated Pods.
Delete one controlled test Pod and verify the controller creates a replacement and restores the requested replica count.
A workload recovery plan must account for dependencies and the recovery capabilities needed to satisfy its objectives.
List the supplied infrastructure, data and service dependencies and place each prerequisite restoration before the steps that depend on it.
Include verification points before dependent services resume so incomplete restoration is not mistaken for usable recovery.
Logs Insights queries select and transform log events using commands connected with pipe characters.
Select the log group and time window, then use fields @timestamp, @message, REQUEST_FIELD | filter REQUEST_FIELD = "ID" | sort @timestamp asc with the actual supplied request field and identity.
Use shared request identity and event timestamps to reconstruct the supplied symptom’s sequence, retaining the relevant events as evidence.
An alarm action can publish state-change notifications to an SNS topic without changing the alarm’s metric evaluation.
Configure the approved topic as the alarm’s notification action and create the approved recipient subscription, confirming it when required.
Verify the recipient receives a test alarm notification containing alarm and workload context; a configured but unconfirmed subscription may not deliver notifications.
A Lambda execution role grants the function permission to access AWS resources during invocation.
Assign the approved execution role whose actions and resources are limited to the supplied operational task.
Invoke the function with the supplied payload and inspect its returned result and execution logs, distinguishing successful invocation from a successful operational result.
A GuardDuty finding contains a finding type, severity, affected resource and details of suspicious activity.
Inspect resource identity, activity timestamps and finding details, and preserve the evidence supporting investigation.
Follow the established investigation and escalation procedure for the finding type rather than taking destructive action from severity alone.
S3 bucket policies can grant or deny object operations to specified principals and resource paths.
Give approved audit writers and readers only their required actions on the intended bucket or object ARNs; inspect other applicable grants and denies.
Test a write and read with approved identities and a read with the unapproved identity; encryption or retention settings do not replace authorization checks.
SSE-KMS encrypts S3 objects with an AWS KMS key, while SSE-S3 uses S3-managed keys.
Reading an SSE-KMS object requires both s3:GetObject permission and kms:Decrypt authority for its key; SSE-S3 does not require KMS key-use permission.
Configure the supplied KMS key as bucket default encryption and test reads with approved object/key authority and with KMS use denied; inspect the object’s encryption metadata.

misconceptions.statement: Changing bucket default encryption does not re-encrypt objects that already exist; their individual encryption settings still matter.

required_facts.statement: A Terraform plan describes proposed additions, updates, deletions and replacements based on configuration, state and observed infrastructure.
Create a saved plan with terraform plan -out=PLAN_FILE and inspect it with terraform show PLAN_FILE; replacement includes destruction and creation, not merely an in-place update.

Compare affected resource identities and every proposed action, including the mandatory deletion case, with the supplied scope and impact criteria and record accept or block with plan evidence; review does not require destructive execution.

For EC2 API operations that support DryRun, the dry-run request checks permissions without executing the operation; DryRunOperation indicates sufficient permission and UnauthorizedOperation indicates insufficient permission.
Use the supplied fleet wrapper’s preview mode, inspect its proposed targets and actions and compare them with approved scope without enabling mutation.
Dry-run permission success does not guarantee later operation success or provide a universal preview of every AWS service’s changes.
A fleet command has separate invocation results for individual targets, which may differ within one command.
Inspect invocation statuses and outputs and record successful, failed and unresolved targets separately.
Use target-specific results to choose the scoped follow-up rather than blindly repeating the entire operation on already successful targets.
Temporary credentials stop being usable after expiration and must be replaced with a newly authorized session.
On an expired-session error, renew the approved session through its credential provider and use the new access key, secret key and token together.
Before retrying a resource-changing operation, inspect its known outcome and use a supported idempotency token where the supplied operation offers one to avoid duplicate effects.
The ECS task role supplies credentials for AWS calls made by the application containers.
The task execution role authorizes ECS startup work such as pulling an image and publishing logs; it is distinct from application AWS permissions.
Set taskRoleArn to the approved least-privilege application role in the task definition and test allowed and denied application operations from the task.
A governed account baseline applies standardized organizational controls and configuration to accounts.
Apply the supplied approved control configuration to the sandbox account and inspect each stated control’s deployment or evaluation result.
Distinguish preventive controls that restrict actions from detective controls that report noncompliance when interpreting the baseline checks.
A ConfigMap supplies nonconfidential configuration separately from the container image.
Reference a ConfigMap with envFrom.configMapRef or env.valueFrom.configMapKeyRef in the supplied Pod template.
Reference a Secret with env.valueFrom.secretKeyRef or a secret-backed volume and test the consuming workload without printing the secret values.
Secrets require access control and appropriate storage protection; base64 encoding is not encryption.

misconceptions.statement: Environment variables populated from a ConfigMap do not automatically update inside already-running containers when the ConfigMap changes.

required_facts.statement: A pipeline has stages containing actions that pass declared input and output artifacts between source, build and deployment operations.
Configure source output, CodeBuild input/output and CodeDeploy input artifact names so each action receives the intended revision’s output.
The CodePipeline service role requires trust for codepipeline.amazonaws.com and permissions for its actions and artifact access; this service role is not GitHub OIDC federation.
Verify action execution evidence carries the intended source revision through deployment and a failed action prevents normal progression to dependent actions.
The same CloudFormation template can provision equivalent resource declarations in multiple approved target environments.

For each approved account/Region pair, use a named role profile with role_arn and source_profile, verify its caller with aws sts get-caller-identity --profile NAME, and create the supplied stack with that profile and explicit --region REGION.
Inspect stack outputs and S3 bucket identity and location in every intended target and check the supplied unapproved targets received no stack.
The subnet’s route table must contain a matching destination route to a usable target for the required network path.
Check DNS resolution and the intended endpoint address using the supplied tools, then inspect route association, required protocol/port rules and response traffic to localize the failing layer.
Network ACLs are stateless, so required requests and responses need permitted traffic in their respective directions.
Make the approved correction supported by the failing layer’s evidence and repeat the endpoint connection test.
Patch Manager uses patch baselines and managed-node targets to scan or install patches and report compliance.
Use the established maintenance-window task with the approved target set, patch document parameters, concurrency and error limits.
Inspect task execution and per-node patch compliance results to verify which approved instances were patched and which require follow-up.
A Kubernetes Service provides a stable network endpoint for a changing set of selected Pods.
Set spec.selector to match the intended Pod labels and ports.port and ports.targetPort to map the Service port to the application’s container port.
Apply the supplied Service, inspect its EndpointSlices or endpoints and test the Service address from the supplied client to verify selected Pods receive traffic.
Controlled failure experiments test how a system behaves under disruption rather than merely inspecting its configuration.
Define the approved fault, limited scope, expected signals and abort conditions before injecting the sandbox failure.
Observe alarm state history and receipt of the expected notification during the fault, then remove the fault and verify recovery.
A published Lambda version is an immutable snapshot of function code and most configuration.
A Lambda alias points to a published version and can be updated to direct invocations to a different version.

Use aws lambda publish-version --function-name NAME, then aws lambda update-alias --function-name NAME --name ALIAS --function-version VERSION; invoke NAME:ALIAS through the supplied test and roll back by updating the alias to the approved previous version.
Changing a Deployment’s Pod template creates a new rollout revision; scaling alone does not create a new template revision.
Use kubectl set image deployment/NAME CONTAINER=IMAGE to update the supplied image and kubectl rollout status deployment/NAME to monitor rollout.
On the controlled failure, inspect rollout history and use kubectl rollout undo deployment/NAME --to-revision=REVISION to restore the approved prior revision and verify readiness.
An EC2 blue/green deployment installs a revision on replacement instances before rerouting traffic from the original instances.
Use the supplied blue/green deployment group, replacement fleet and load balancer configuration and verify lifecycle and health evidence before the approved traffic rerouting.
Use the supplied rollback configuration or redeployment procedure and verify traffic and application behavior return to the known-good revision.
A Python finally block runs cleanup when control leaves its try block, including when an exception is raised.
Wrap the supplied failing task in try: ... finally: ... and put the supplied scoped cleanup calls in finally.
Track resources created by the exercise and clean up only those resources, then verify their removal and preservation of preexisting resources.
Terraform normally refreshes tracked resources before planning, revealing out-of-band changes relevant to the proposed actions.
After the supplied drift, compare observed instance settings with configuration and decide whether to restore the declaration or update it to reflect an approved intended change.
Generate and inspect a new plan, run the supplied approval/apply workflow and verify live instance settings match the chosen declaration.

A refresh-only plan proposes state and output updates to reflect remote changes; applying the approved refresh-only plan persists those updates without restoring remote infrastructure to configuration.
A module packages resource declarations behind input variables and output values.
Configure module "NAME" with the supplied source and named input arguments; reference its output as module.NAME.OUTPUT.
Initialize the module, inspect the input values and planned instance settings, apply through the approved workflow and verify the created instance and declared outputs.
Rightsizing matches resource type and size to workload performance and capacity requirements rather than simply choosing the smallest instance.
Compare supplied load, utilization and performance evidence with service constraints and recommend a smaller instance only when those constraints remain satisfied.
Account for peak and changing demand in the baseline rather than using one low-utilization sample as sufficient evidence.
A finding’s resource identity, severity and activity details provide context needed by the accountable responder.
Route the supplied finding ID or evidence link, affected resource, observed activity and urgency to the responsible owner and apply the established escalation path.
Preserve the finding evidence rather than replacing it with an unsupported claim that the resource is compromised.
An EventBridge rule pairs an event pattern with one or more targets to receive matching events.
Set the supplied event bus and pattern and add only the approved SNS or Systems Manager target and required target parameters.
Configure the target’s required permissions, then send matching and nonmatching test events and inspect the approved target’s execution or notification evidence.
An ECS service maintains the desired number of tasks and replaces tasks that stop or fail.
Create the service with the supplied cluster, task definition, network settings and desiredCount.
Remove one task in the controlled exercise and inspect service events and running/pending task counts until the desired count is restored.
A nonzero command exit status reports failure to a pipeline step, while zero reports success.
Run the supplied unit and integration test commands in workflow steps with run: TEST_COMMAND; set the promotion job’s needs: [UNIT_JOB, INTEGRATION_JOB] to require both test jobs.
Do not set continue-on-error on the blocking test steps; demonstrate a failing supplied test prevents the dependent promotion.
Small coherent changes reduce review complexity and make delivery feedback easier to act on.

In the supplied repository workflow, stage the focused files with git add FILES, commit with git commit -m "MESSAGE", push the review branch with git push, and open its supplied pull-request interface to request review.
Submit a focused infrastructure pull request with its intent, coherent diff and saved plan evidence showing the affected EC2 resource.
After the supplied approval, execute the supplied CI apply using the approved saved plan and attach the execution and resource-verification evidence to the change record.
Resilience testing deliberately introduces failures to verify the workload can meet its availability requirements.
Limit the approved failure to the supplied AZ components, define abort criteria, and monitor client-visible service behavior during the experiment.
Check that the remaining independent capacity and request path maintain the required service behavior rather than inferring availability from surviving instance count alone.
Resource deletion must respect dependencies; CloudFormation uses resource relationships when deleting a stack.
Identify only the supplied exercise resources by stack membership or approved tags, remove dependent resources before their prerequisites and verify deletion results.
An S3 bucket must be empty before deletion; remove the exercise bucket’s objects, all object versions and delete markers before deleting that bucket.
Retained resources and failed deletions need explicit inspection and approved follow-up; a completed deletion operation is not billing verification.
Recovery execution needs a valid, unexpired session with the permissions required for backup access and resource creation.
Establish the approved recovery session, inspect its identity and expiry, and test the supplied backup-read and recovery-resource operations before rehearsal.
A valid credential lifetime does not prove sufficient authorization; verify both access outcomes and lifetime.
Recovery testing should use a controlled environment that limits the experiment’s effects.
Prepare the supplied isolated account and network target and check restoration destinations and client test traffic do not point to production.
Record the approved scope and stop conditions before provisioning recovery resources or directing test traffic.
An aws:approve Automation step pauses execution pending approval or rejection by the designated approvers.
Put the approval step before the protected operation and use the supplied branching or failure path to prevent that operation on rejection or stop.
Stop an Automation execution with the approved stop operation when a stop condition occurs and inspect execution state before allowing further actions.
Automation execution details include an execution identifier, step statuses, inputs, outputs and failure information.
Record execution ID, acting role, target identities, start/end times and per-step outcomes for the supplied response.
Use CloudTrail request identity and operation evidence to attribute the underlying AWS actions; success and failure outcomes both belong in the response record.
CloudTrail log-file integrity validation uses signed digest files and hashes to detect modification or deletion of delivered log files.

Run aws cloudtrail validate-logs --trail-arn ARN --start-time TIME --end-time TIME --region REGION against the supplied log/digest interval and inspect validation failures; for an organization trail also provide the required --account-id.
Digest validation supplies tamper evidence but does not itself prevent unauthorized access or deletion.
S3 Object Lock applies retention to object versions using governance or compliance mode and a retain-until date.
Apply the supplied default retention duration and mode on the prepared Object Lock bucket and inspect individual audit-object version retention.
Compliance mode prevents deletion or shortening of retention during the retention period even by root; governance mode permits bypass only with the necessary bypass authorization and request.
The S3 backend stores Terraform state in a specified bucket and key, separate from the configuration that declares managed resources.
Provision the protected backend bucket with the supplied local-state bootstrap configuration before selecting it as the backend.
Run terraform init -migrate-state after changing the backend, approve the supplied migration and verify state is at the intended bucket/key.
By default Terraform destroys an object before creating its replacement; create_before_destroy requests the reverse order where supported.
prevent_destroy rejects a plan that would destroy the protected resource while that lifecycle rule remains in its configuration.

Set the supplied lifecycle argument in the resource block, introduce the controlled replacement-triggering change, and inspect the plan’s replacement order or prevention error before the approved permitted apply.
Lifecycle settings constrain replacement mechanics but do not replace scope and impact approval.
Creating a stack from a template provisions its declared resources under the target account’s execution authority and selected Region.
Use the supplied restoration template, approved recovery credentials, explicit isolated target and required parameters to create the replacement EC2 stack.
Monitor stack events until creation completes, inspect resource IDs and outputs, and run the supplied instance and service recovery-ready checks.
Inspector findings report vulnerability evidence, affected resources and severity that can inform release decisions.
Compare the supplied scan report with the stated severity threshold and documented exception policy to decide whether a finding is actionable.
Make the scan-policy check return failure for an actionable unexcepted finding and require its success before promotion; retain the report and policy decision as evidence.
Pipeline execution and action history identify failed actions and their error details.
Find the first failing action in the selected execution, inspect its input artifact revision and linked service logs, and use the error evidence to identify the correction.
Retest after the approved correction and verify that action succeeds before investigating later dependent actions that did not run.
EC2 system status checks concern underlying AWS host issues, while instance checks concern the instance’s software and networking.
Use the supplied metric and log time window to identify the affected workload, then inspect the component’s service status, events and logs rather than assuming the symptom proves its cause.
For a container, inspect container state, exit status and recent logs; apply the evidence-supported correction and repeat the supplied health check.
A post-deployment validation action checks live application behavior rather than merely whether a deployment operation completed.
Run the supplied smoke-check action against the deployed endpoint and verify the expected response for the deployed revision.

In the supplied Lambda validation action, call CodePipeline PutJobSuccessResult with the job ID only after a passing smoke check; call PutJobFailureResult on failure so dependent progression remains blocked.
EventBridge retries retryable target-delivery failures within configured maximum event age and retry-attempt limits.
Configure the target RetryPolicy MaximumRetryAttempts and MaximumEventAgeInSeconds to the approved finite budget.
Configure DeadLetterConfig with the approved SQS queue ARN and required queue permissions, then inspect a seeded exhausted delivery failure in that queue.
Some nonretryable delivery failures go directly to failure capture; retry configuration does not guarantee every failure receives retries.
An ECS rolling deployment replaces service tasks according to minimumHealthyPercent and maximumPercent relative to desiredCount.
Register the supplied new image version in a task-definition revision and update the service to that revision.
Inspect service events, running task revisions and health until the supplied steady-state criteria are met; a service-update request alone is not proof of a healthy rollout.
The build stage produces a build artifact; release combines that build with environment configuration, and run executes the release.
Promote the same immutable artifact reference or digest to the next environment while supplying that environment’s configuration rather than rebuilding the source.
Compare the deployed artifact digests in staging and production and their recorded build provenance to verify the tested output is the promoted output.
Cost Explorer data is refreshed at least once every 24 hours and some data can take longer to appear.
Inspect the supplied teardown interval with account and service or usage-type filters and compare usage timestamps with resource-deletion evidence.
Distinguish charges for usage before deletion from evidence of continuing usage and repeat the check after the billing data refresh rather than declaring zero cost from resource absence.
S3 backend access needs permissions for the selected state bucket and object key; state can contain sensitive values.
Scope approved readers and writers to the required ListBucket prefix and GetObject/PutObject state object operations, with supplied locking permissions configured separately.
Initialize the supplied backend, provision the separate exercise bucket through the approved identity, and test that an unapproved identity cannot read or overwrite state.
State access isolation prevents unauthorized access; it is separate from the mechanism that coordinates concurrent authorized writers.
The S3 backend supports lock-file locking when use_lockfile = true; locking is opt-in.
Set use_lockfile = true in the supplied S3 backend configuration and use the supplied s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject and s3:DeleteObject permissions on the .tflock object.
During the controlled state-changing operation that holds the lock, attempt a competing operation and verify it cannot acquire the lock or change state; do not disable locking to bypass the test.
Locking coordinates concurrent state writers; it is not an authorization boundary against identities that can directly change state objects.

misconceptions.statement: Force-unlock is not a safe way to bypass another active state writer; it is reserved for a lock from a failed operation when automatic unlocking failed.

required_facts.statement: A manual approval action stops pipeline progression until an authorized approver approves; rejection or expiration fails the action.
Place an approval action between staging and production with the supplied review link or revision context and authorized approver permissions.
Verify the pipeline stops at approval and advances only after approval of the intended execution and revision.

misconceptions.statement: Receiving an approval notification does not itself grant permission to approve the action; approval requires the appropriate authorization.

required_facts.statement: A runbook describes known procedures and their expected operational outcomes.
Verify the established runbook’s preconditions, execute only the approved actions and check each expected result before advancing.
On a supplied stop condition or an outcome outside the runbook’s bounds, stop routine execution and escalate with the observed evidence.
Recovery verification must test both restoration time against RTO and recoverable data loss against RPO.
Using the supplied timestamps, measure elapsed time from the defined disruption start to passing service-readiness checks and compare it with RTO.

Using the supplied recovery markers, measure the gap between the disruption point and the latest recovered data point and compare it with RPO; a running service alone does not prove either objective was met.
Post-incident analysis documents the incident’s impact, events, contributing causes and actions to reduce recurrence.
Write a timeline from supplied evidence and distinguish direct observations from causal conclusions supported by the verified fix.
Record one preventive action justified by the demonstrated cause, with an accountable owner and a way to verify completion.
Recovery procedures include restoring service and directing clients to the recovered environment.
Confirm the restored target’s supplied readiness checks pass, perform the approved DNS or application endpoint switch and verify clients reach the restored target.
For DNS cutover, account for cached answers and TTL when testing client convergence rather than assuming every client immediately uses the new endpoint.
A list is a mutable sequence, suitable for ordered positional access with updates.
A tuple is an immutable sequence, suitable for a fixed ordered group of values.
A set stores distinct hashable values without sequence positions and supports membership tests and set operations.
A dictionary maps hashable keys to values, supports updates and preserves insertion order; use it for lookup by key rather than by sequence position.
input(prompt) displays an optional prompt and returns entered text without its trailing newline.
print(value1, value2, ...) displays values separated by a space by default and ends with a newline; sep and end customize those delimiters.
enumerate(sequence, start=0) supplies pairs of a counter and the corresponding element; the counter starts at zero by default.
Use for position, value in enumerate(sequence, start=1): with an indented body to number entries from one without updating a manual counter.
Many decimal fractions cannot be represented exactly as binary floating-point values.
math.isclose(a, b, rel_tol=..., abs_tol=...) compares values using relative and absolute tolerances rather than exact equality.
The default relative tolerance is 1e-9 and absolute tolerance is 0.0; comparison to zero requires an appropriate positive absolute tolerance when nonzero differences should count as close.
A compound statement’s header ends with a colon and its multi-line suite is an indented block; nested suites require deeper indentation.
Indentation determines statement grouping; dedenting ends a deeper group, and inconsistent indentation can be invalid.
Use four spaces for each indentation level when repairing block structure.
After import math, math.sqrt(x) returns the square root of x.
math functions operate on real rather than complex values; an invalid operation such as sqrt(-1.0) raises ValueError.
A collection can contain other collections; successive indices and keys select progressively nested values.
Assign to the final selected list index or dictionary key to update that nested value.
Place an indented inner for loop in an outer for loop to traverse the inner collection for each outer item.
For nested rows, for row in rows: with a nested for cell in row: visits each row’s cells before proceeding to the next row.
range(stop) starts at zero with step one; range(start, stop, step) uses the specified start and nonzero step.
The stop value is excluded; a positive step continues below stop and a negative step continues above stop.
Use for index in range(start, stop, 2): to traverse every second integer position in an increasing interval.
Invoke an explicitly chosen Python executable with a script path as its argument to execute the script.
print sends script output to the standard output stream by default.
A zero process exit status indicates successful termination and a nonzero status abnormal termination; sys.exit(status) requests that status.
An expression statement evaluates an expression; in interactive mode its non-None value is displayed.
An assignment evaluates its right-hand expression before binding the resulting value to its target.
Python evaluates expressions from left to right; operator precedence and parentheses determine how constituent operations group.
A # outside a string starts a comment extending to the physical line’s end; comments are ignored by syntax.
Keep comments accurate when code changes, because a comment contradicting code is worse than no comment.
Use inline comments sparingly and explain a useful reason rather than restating an obvious operation.
Starting the interpreter without a script enters interactive mode, with >>> for a new command and ... for continuation.
Entering an expression displays its result, and a variable assigned in the session can be used by later expressions.
Type commands without copying the prompt characters; lines without prompts in tutorial examples are output.
Source can be compiled to a code object; invalid source syntax raises SyntaxError.
In CPython, the compiler produces bytecode used by the interpreter; bytecode is an implementation detail, not a cross-implementation guarantee.
Top-level module statements execute when the module is first imported or when its file is executed as a script.
At runtime, an assignment evaluates its expression using current values and binds the result to its target.
Expressions inside parentheses, square brackets or braces may span physical lines without backslashes.
Keep the delimiters and expression intact when splitting a long call across lines; continuation indentation does not determine block grouping.
Align continuation arguments with the opening delimiter or use a hanging indent.
text.strip() returns text with leading and trailing whitespace removed; it does not remove interior whitespace.
The optional chars argument to strip is a set of removable characters, not a literal prefix or suffix.
text.lower() returns a copy with cased characters converted to lowercase.
text.split(separator) separates on that delimiter and preserves empty fields between repeated delimiters.
text.split() without a separator splits on runs of whitespace and omits leading and trailing empty fields.
Syntax errors occur while parsing source; the error report identifies the line and location where the parser detected invalid syntax.
Syntactically valid code can raise an exception during execution; its error message identifies the exception type and explanation.
Invalid syntax prevents the source from compiling to an executable code object, so repair the syntax before tracing that source’s runtime behavior.
False, None, numeric zero and empty built-in strings and collections have false truth values; nonzero numbers and nonempty built-in strings and collections have true truth values.
Use if collection: for a nonempty guard or if not collection: for an empty guard; truth testing does not require equality to True.
None is the singleton object commonly used to represent absence of a value.
is tests whether operands are the same object and is not tests whether they are different objects.
Use value is None or value is not None to test absence rather than a truth test that would also reject a legitimate zero or empty value.
str contains Unicode text, distinct from binary bytes.
text.encode("utf-8") produces bytes using UTF-8.
payload.decode("utf-8") produces text from UTF-8 bytes; the decoding encoding must match the encoded data to recover that text.
A decoding failure raises UnicodeDecodeError when the supplied bytes are not valid for the chosen decoding.
zip(left, right) pairs corresponding elements into tuples for parallel traversal.
Use for left_item, right_item in zip(left, right): to process each pair in an indented body.
By default zip stops at the shortest input, omitting unmatched trailing values from longer inputs.
Assignment can bind multiple names to the same object rather than copying it; mutating a shared list or dictionary can be visible through other names and to a function’s caller.
items.copy() or items[:] creates a shallow copy of a list, allowing independent changes to that list’s top-level items.
A shallow copy still contains references to the original elements, so a nested mutable element can remain shared.
After from collections import Counter, Counter(items) counts occurrences of hashable elements in a mapping from elements to counts.
counts.most_common(1) returns a list with the most frequent element and its count, or an empty list for an empty counter.
most_common orders pairs by descending count, with ties ordered by first encounter; access the first returned pair only if the result is nonempty.
print(label, value) displays a label and a value to reveal the state at that execution point.
repr(value) returns a printable representation that can expose details obscured by ordinary string display.
Place diagnostic output after the binding or before the operation being investigated to observe that current value; removing the print call removes that diagnostic output.
Document public functions, modules, classes and methods with docstrings.
Place a string literal first in a function body to provide its docstring, with a concise purpose summary and additional calling-convention details after a blank line.
Document the function’s arguments, return values and applicable exceptions as part of its interface.
help(function) displays documentation for the function, including its docstring and signature.
BaseException is the root of the built-in exception hierarchy, and Exception is its subclass for ordinary application failures.
ValueError and OSError are subclasses of Exception, and FileNotFoundError is a subclass of OSError.
KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit and GeneratorExit are directly under BaseException rather than under Exception.
A raised exception skips the remaining operations in its current try body and searches for a matching handler.
Handler matching accepts an exception of the named class or a subclass; handlers are examined in their written order.
If no local handler matches, the exception propagates through the callers to an outer handler, or becomes unhandled if none matches.
When a handler recovers, execution continues after its try/except statement, not at the failed operation.
Place release operations in an aligned finally: body following try: to run them when leaving the protected operation.
finally executes on normal completion, on an exception and on a return from the try body.
An unhandled exception is re-raised after finally completes normally; a return from finally can replace a pending return or suppress a pending exception.
A function definition creates a function object bound to its name; the bare name refers to the function and name(arguments) calls it.
Functions can be passed where a function object is required.
A callable can be stored and invoked later.
A receiving helper can call a supplied function parameter using parameter(value), rather than passing the result of an earlier call.
A nested function can resolve a free name in an enclosing function scope; each call has its own local bindings.
A returned nested function can use enclosing values after its creating call has finished.
Declare nonlocal name in a nested function to rebind an existing name in the nearest enclosing function scope.
A stateful factory can bind state in its body and return a nested function that reads and rebinds that state with nonlocal.
from pathlib import Path provides concrete paths using the platform’s path conventions.
base / "child" constructs a child path; an absolute right operand replaces the previous path rather than remaining underneath it.
Relative paths are interpreted against the current working directory; choosing an explicit base directory avoids relying on an unintended working directory.
Use raise ExceptionType(message) to signal a particular failure with explanatory context.
ValueError indicates an argument of an appropriate type but an inappropriate value, apart from cases with a more precise exception.
Use specific exceptions to permit precise handling.
The final line of an exception report gives the exception type and message.
The traceback’s preceding frames give source locations and the calling context where the exception occurred.
Traceback frames in a call chain lead down to the most recent failing operation; use its displayed file, line and statement to locate the immediate cause.
breakpoint() enters the debugger at the call site; by default it invokes pdb.set_trace().
In pdb, p expression prints an expression’s value, and l lists nearby source lines.
n executes the next line without stepping into a called function, s steps into calls, and c continues until another breakpoint or termination.
Use b line_number to set a breakpoint and inspect the values controlling a suspect branch when execution pauses there.
Default argument values are evaluated once at definition time, so a mutable default can retain modifications across calls.
Use a None default and an if parameter is None: branch that creates a new list or dictionary in the function body to obtain fresh per-call state.
sorted(records, key=function) returns a new sorted list and uses function(record) as each record’s comparison key.
sorted does not mutate the original list; reverse=True reverses the ordering.
Sorting is stable: items with equal keys retain their original relative order.
str.lower can provide a lowercase text key for case-normalized ordering.
lambda parameters: expression creates an anonymous function whose result is the single expression’s value.
A lambda is restricted to one expression and can be passed as key=lambda item: expression to sorting.
An except handler matches its named exception class and subclasses; the first matching handler runs.
Order subclass-specific handlers before broader parent handlers so the specific recovery remains reachable.
FileNotFoundError is a subclass of OSError, so except FileNotFoundError: must precede except OSError: when their recovery actions differ.
ValueError can identify an unsuitable value such as malformed numeric input; reject or request correction of an input that violates the stated value contract.
NameError means a local or global name cannot be found; a misspelled implementation name calls for code correction rather than rejection of the supplied input.
PermissionError reports inadequate access rights for a filesystem operation; report the access failure rather than assuming the supplied path or implementation is inherently wrong.
In a function definition, *args collects remaining positional arguments into a tuple.
In a function definition, **kwargs collects additional keyword arguments into a dictionary; a parameter may not receive two values in a call.
In a call, *args expands a sequence into positional arguments and **kwargs expands a dictionary into keyword arguments.
A forwarding wrapper can define def wrapper(*args, **kwargs): and return target(*args, **kwargs), avoiding additional arguments that duplicate a supplied binding.
open(path, "r") reads an existing file; r is the default mode.
open(path, "w") writes and truncates an existing file, or creates a new file.
open(path, "a") appends to an existing file or creates it.
open(path, "x") exclusively creates a new file and fails if it exists.
Handle FileExistsError when exclusive creation finds an existing destination, rather than changing to a truncating mode unintentionally.
If a class defines __init__, instantiation automatically invokes it on the new instance and passes the constructor arguments.
Define def __init__(self, first, second): in the class and assign self.first = first and self.second = second to initialize those instance attributes.
__init__ initializes the created instance rather than returning a replacement object.
An instance method receives the target instance as its first argument, conventionally named self.
Define def method(self, argument): inside the class and use self.attribute to read or reassign that instance’s state.
instance.method(value) passes instance implicitly as self and value as the next argument.
An instance method receives the instance as its implicit first argument and can use that instance’s state.
Put @classmethod above def method(cls, ...): to receive the class as the implicit first argument; return cls(arguments) to construct an instance in an alternative constructor.
Put @staticmethod above def method(...): for an operation with no implicit instance or class argument.
Instance data attributes can hold collaborator objects.
Store a collaborator as self.collaborator and invoke self.collaborator.method(arguments) from an instance method to delegate work to that object.
A leading underscore conventionally marks a non-public implementation name; it does not enforce access protection.
Python does not provide truly inaccessible private instance attributes through this naming convention.
Public attributes form the interface expected to be used by clients; keep implementation details non-public with a leading underscore.
Expose a public method that operates on the receiving instance’s supporting attributes instead of requiring callers to manage that state directly.
Define class Derived(Base): to inherit from Base; an overridden method replaces the inherited method for ordinary lookup on Derived instances.
Inside an ordinary derived instance method, super().method(arguments) delegates lookup to the next class in method resolution order.
In a derived __init__, call super().__init__(arguments) to run inherited initialization before adding derived initialization where required.
Define an application-specific exception as a class derived from Exception, using class CustomError(Exception): with an indented pass body.
raise CustomError(message) signals that custom failure; except CustomError: handles it at a surrounding boundary.
Class variables hold attributes shared by instances, while instance variables hold data unique to an instance.
A mutable list assigned in the class body is shared unless shadowed by an instance attribute.
Assign self.items = [] in __init__ to create a separate list for each instance rather than mutating a shared class list.
json.dumps(value) serializes supported Python values to a JSON str.
json.loads(text) deserializes a JSON string into Python values.
Default conversions support dictionaries, lists, tuples, strings, numeric values, booleans and None; lists and tuples both encode as arrays, which decode as lists.
JSON object keys are strings, so non-string dictionary keys need not retain their original Python types on a round trip.
type(object) returns the object’s type.
isinstance(object, Class) checks whether the object is an instance of that class or one of its subclasses.
dir(object) attempts to list relevant attribute names, but is not guaranteed to be complete.
getattr(object, name) retrieves a named attribute, with an optional fallback if it is absent.
Attribute names beginning with an underscore conventionally signal internal use rather than a public interface.
directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) creates the directory and missing parents, allowing an existing directory; both options default to False.
directory.iterdir() traverses its immediate entries in arbitrary order.
source.rename(target) renames or moves the entry to target; a relative target is resolved against the current working directory, not against source’s parent.
rename can silently replace an existing target file on Unix when permitted, while Windows raises FileExistsError for an existing target.
Construct the destination as directory / filename to target the selected output directory rather than relying on a bare relative filename.
Define def __repr__(self): returning a str for an information-rich, unambiguous representation used by repr and interactive inspection.
Define def __str__(self): returning a str for a convenient user-facing representation used by str and print.
If __str__ is not defined, the default representation uses __repr__.
Use open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") to decode UTF-8 text and open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") to encode written text explicitly.
The encoding argument specifies the text encoding; the selected encoding must match the file’s bytes for correct decoding.
A UnicodeDecodeError indicates a decoding failure, which can arise when the file’s bytes are invalid for the selected encoding.
FileNotFoundError indicates that the requested file or directory does not exist; handle it separately from content problems.
UnicodeDecodeError indicates failure to decode the content using the selected encoding.
csv.Error reports errors detected by the CSV parser; except csv.Error: can provide a parsing-failure response.

DictReader fills missing fields with restval, defaulting to None, and places excess fields under restkey, defaulting to None; validate required row fields explicitly rather than assuming malformed row lengths raise csv.Error.
Wrap the import at a boundary with specific exception handlers for missing files, decoding and parser failures, and report each according to its cause.
Use with context_expression as resource: followed by an indented body; the context manager enters before the body and exits after it.
Once entry succeeds, the exit method runs whether the body completes normally or raises an exception; a context manager may suppress an exception.
For with open(path) as f:, leaving the body closes the file, including when the body raises.
The b mode selects binary I/O: open(path, "rb") reads bytes and open(path, "wb") writes bytes rather than str.
wb creates or truncates the destination file.
Read a binary payload with source.read() and write that bytes value with destination.write(payload) to copy it without text decoding.
Use managed opening with with to close both files after the copy.
datetime.strptime(text, format) parses text according to an explicit format, and .date() obtains its calendar date.
Use %Y-%m-%d for a year-month-day numeric date.
Subtracting one date from another returns a timedelta representing their difference.
For calendar dates, (later_date - earlier_date).days gives their signed day difference.

optional_enrichment.statement: Subtract datetime values only with compatible timezone awareness: two naive values or two aware values; mixing naive and aware values raises TypeError.

required_facts.statement: A module is a file of Python definitions and statements, with a .py suffix; its filename without that suffix supplies the module name.
Move a shared helper definition into a sibling module, then import module and call module.helper(arguments), or use from module import helper.
In ordinary script invocation, the script’s directory is included in the module search path, permitting sibling-module imports.
A regular package groups modules in a directory containing __init__.py; that file may be empty.
Use import package.module and package.module.helper(arguments), or from package.module import helper, to access a packaged helper.
After import logging, logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) obtains a logger named for the module.

DEBUG is for detailed diagnostics, INFO for expected progress, WARNING for an unexpected condition while operation continues, ERROR for inability to perform a function, and CRITICAL for a serious failure.
Emit events with logger.debug(message) or logger.info(message), choosing a method corresponding to the desired level.
Configure application logging with logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO) to include INFO and higher events; the default root threshold is WARNING.
Propagation normally passes events to ancestor handlers; attaching handlers to both a logger and its ancestors can duplicate output, so ordinarily configure a handler at one suitable ancestor.
A module executed as the main script has __name__ equal to "__main__"; an imported module has its module name instead.
Put command-interface actions under if __name__ == "__main__": so importing the module does not execute those actions.
Keep reusable helper definitions outside that guarded command-interface body so importers can use them.
After import argparse, create parser = argparse.ArgumentParser() to define a command interface.
parser.add_argument("input_path") declares a required positional value, while a name starting with -- declares an option.
parser.add_argument("--verbose", action="store_true") creates a boolean flag that defaults to False and becomes True when present.
args = parser.parse_args() parses the command line into attributes such as args.input_path and args.verbose.
By default invalid arguments produce an error message and exit status 2; missing required arguments are invalid.
After checking built-in modules, an ordinary import searches sys.path for the named module; the script directory normally comes before standard-library directories.
A local file with the same name as a standard-library module can shadow that module; rename the conflicting local file to remove that ambiguity.
Inspect sys.path to see the search locations used by the interpreter.
Inspect module.__file__ to locate a file-backed imported module.
os.environ maps process environment names to string values.
os.environ.get("SETTING", fallback) returns the configured string or fallback if the name is absent; without a fallback it returns None for absence.
For a required setting, check absence explicitly or use bracket lookup, which raises KeyError for a missing key; report missing configuration instead of proceeding with an unintended value.
random is designed for modelling and simulation, while secrets provides cryptographically strong randomness for security-sensitive values.
random.seed(seed) initializes the pseudo-random generator; reuse a seed to reproduce a sequence under the documented reproducibility conditions.
random.random() returns a floating-point value in the half-open interval from 0.0 to 1.0.
secrets.token_hex(nbytes) generates a random hexadecimal token for security-sensitive use.
A regular expression describes a text pattern; [...] selects one character from a set, ranges such as A-Z select a range, and * allows zero or more repetitions.
Concatenated pattern elements match in sequence; a raw string literal such as r"..." avoids Python string-escape processing of pattern backslashes.
re.fullmatch(pattern, text) returns a Match if the whole text matches and None otherwise; test is not None for successful validation.
re.match checks at the beginning, while re.search looks for a match anywhere; neither requires the entire text to match.
sys.executable gives the running interpreter’s executable path when available; it may be an empty string or None if Python cannot retrieve it.
sys.version gives the interpreter version plus build and compiler information.
After import sys, print(sys.executable) and print(sys.version) display which runtime is actually executing the code.
Run the selected Python executable with -m venv .venv to create a project environment, containing bin/python on POSIX or Scripts/python.exe on Windows.
Activation changes command lookup to the environment’s executable, but activation is not required when invoking that executable by its full path.
sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix identifies an interpreter running in a virtual environment.
Run the environment’s Python with -m pip list to inspect its installed packages.
Virtual environments are isolated from base-environment packages by default.
Inspect sys.executable in the executed program to identify its actual interpreter, rather than relying on an environment label.
A venv supplies its interpreter at bin/python on POSIX or Scripts/python.exe on Windows.
Configure an execution tool to invoke the intended venv executable explicitly when command lookup selects the wrong Python; activation is not required for explicit executable invocation.
Check sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix and the executable path again after changing the selected runtime.
Invoke the intended environment’s interpreter with -m pip install package_name to install that distribution into that interpreter’s environment.
Use -m pip show package_name or -m pip list through the same interpreter to inspect the installation.
Import the package’s documented import name using the same interpreter to verify it is usable there.
A distribution package installed by pip is not necessarily named the same as the import package used in Python code.
A requirements file lists dependencies, and package_name==version pins a specific version.
Invoke the fresh environment’s Python with -m pip install -r requirements.txt to install the listed requirements.
Use the same interpreter’s -m pip list to inspect installed versions.
Check required imports in the recreated interpreter rather than assuming an installation report proves each module is importable.
assert condition, message raises AssertionError when the condition is false in normal debugging execution.
Python can omit assert statements when optimization is requested with -O, so an assertion must not replace input checks required in production.
Use an explicit conditional and raise for required runtime validation rather than relying on a removable debugging assertion.
An iterable supplies an iterator via iter(value); an iterator supplies successive values via next(iterator) and signals exhaustion with StopIteration.
Separate iter(list_value) calls produce separate traversal state, while the list stores the reusable items.
Calling iter on an iterator returns that same iterator rather than a new independent traversal.
next(iterator, default) returns default when the iterator is exhausted instead of raising StopIteration.
A function containing yield creates a generator iterator when called; advancing it runs until the next yield.
yield value supplies one item and suspends execution, retaining local state until the next advance.
Write a for loop and a condition inside a generator function, yielding each accepted item; reaching the function’s end terminates iteration.
(expression for item in iterable if condition) defines a generator that transforms accepted items lazily; the filtering if clause is optional.
The leftmost iterable expression is evaluated immediately, while item transformations and filtering happen during iteration.
Pass a generator expression as the sole argument to sum to total transformed values without creating an intermediate list.
Each next(iterator) consumes the next available item; a traversal or consumer sees only the remaining items.
Once an iterator raises StopIteration, it must continue to do so on subsequent calls.
iter(iterator) returns the same iterator and does not reset it.
For another pass over a reusable collection, obtain a fresh iterator from that collection rather than reusing its exhausted iterator.
list(iterable) materializes its remaining items into a list that can be traversed repeatedly.
Generator expressions compute values as consumed and tend to use less memory than equivalent list comprehensions.
For a one-pass total, sum(expression for item in iterable) avoids constructing an intermediate transformed list.
An iterator is consumed as it advances and stays exhausted after completion, so repeated reuse may require a stored collection or a new source traversal.
After from itertools import chain, chain(first, second) traverses each input in order, exhausting the first before moving to the second, without first concatenating them into a list.
sum(chain(first, second)) totals numeric items from the combined traversal.
map(function, iterable) lazily applies a callable to successive items and yields the results.
filter(predicate, iterable) lazily yields items for which the predicate is true; filter(None, iterable) keeps truthy items.
filter(predicate, iterable) corresponds to (item for item in iterable if predicate(item)).

[function(item) for item in iterable if predicate(item)] makes a materialized transform-and-filter list and can replace a map/filter composition when that form communicates the computation more clearly.
Use a parenthesized generator expression instead of a list comprehension when preserving lazy traversal is required.
After import unittest, define class Tests(unittest.TestCase): with methods named test_* to express individual supplied checks.
Use self.assertEqual(actual, expected) for equality and self.assertTrue(condition) for a required true condition.
Use with self.assertRaises(ExceptionType): around the supplied failing operation to check that it raises the expected exception.
python -m unittest test_module runs a named test module, and python -m unittest discover invokes test discovery.
Discovery defaults to the current directory and test*.py filenames; -s selects a starting directory and -p selects a filename pattern.
A failure is an unsuccessful assertion check; the runner report identifies the test and traceback for the failed assertion.
An error is an unexpected exception during a test rather than an explicitly failed assertion.
The reported test count records how many tests ran; a count of zero supplies no executed checks of the helper’s behavior.
Define setUp(self) to initialize fresh per-test state before each test method; an error in setUp prevents that test method from running.
tearDown(self) runs after a test when setUp succeeded, including when the test failed.
self.addCleanup(function, *args, **kwargs) registers cleanup that runs after tearDown, or after a failed setUp; registered actions run in reverse registration order.
Register the release callable after acquiring the supplied test resource and store mutable test data on self in setUp rather than in shared class attributes.
Trace each supplied input through the conditions to its actual return; a path reaching the end of a function without a return produces None.
Track each assignment and selected branch in order to determine the actual data and control flow for valid and invalid inputs.
Code from a virtual assistant can be mistaken, so check its behavior rather than treating its generated form as proof of correctness.
Opening a file in w mode truncates existing content; inspect generated mode choices to identify an unintended overwrite.
Path.unlink() removes the file or symbolic link at that path; remove an unintended unlink call instead of executing it.
Path.rename(target) moves an entry and can replace an existing file on Unix; inspect the actual source and destination paths.

An absolute child path replaces a preceding base path, and a relative rename target is interpreted against the working directory; trace these path rules to check the actual destination before execution.
eval evaluates a Python expression and can execute arbitrary code, so it must not be used to process untrusted text.
exec executes Python code supplied as text or a code object and is unsafe for untrusted instructions.
Invoking a shell makes quoting and metacharacters a security responsibility; inspect shell=True and untrusted command construction for injection risk.
Replace execution-based parsing with a parser matching the expected data, such as int or float for numeric text and json.loads for JSON, with explicit validation and handling of malformed input.
Non-executing parsing is not unlimited resource safety: impose input-size limits for untrusted JSON because malicious input can consume substantial CPU and memory.
An official API entry such as sorted documents its signature, keyword-only options and returned value; compare a generated call’s name, arguments and expected result to those documented elements.
Virtual assistants can make mistakes even about Python, so their plausible API claims need checking.
help(object) displays documentation for an available object, supporting inspection of its actual interface in the selected runtime.
Check the executing interpreter’s version when comparing an API claim to version-specific documentation.
